title: A Multimodal Nomogram Predicting the Risk of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson Disease
summary: A multimodal LASSO-Cox model estimated 3-, 5- and 8-year cognitive-impairment risk among Parkinson disease participants initially classified as cognitively normal. In 1,188 participants, 457 developed impairment; nested cross-validation C-index was 0.736 and optimism-corrected C-index 0.733. The model was internally validated in one selected cohort and has no external transport validation. This shares the broad task of Parkinson-related cognitive impairment with an existing diagnostic study, but is a distinct longitudinal prognostic risk model.
ai_technology: LASSO-Cox feature selection and prognostic modeling identify predictors of cognitive impairment.
organization: Virginia Commonwealth University; Parkinson’s Progression Markers Initiative investigators

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: Nested cross-validation, bootstrap optimism correction, calibration and held-out time-dependent AUC analyses were reported.
evidence.unknown: Internal validation in one cohort only; external transportability and clinical benefit have not been established. It is related to active record 2022-05-accuracy-of-machine-learning-using-the-montreal-cognitive-assessment-f, which concerns diagnosis from MoCA rather than longitudinal risk prediction.
